proof.text: Choose an affine open cover $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ and affine covers $U_i\cap U_j=\bigcup_{k\in K_{ij}}V_{ijk}$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Choose these symmetrically, so $K_{ij}=K_{ji}$ and $V_{ijk}=V_{jik}$. Work in the ambient universe $\mathcal V$ of [def-weil-size-convention]; these are small sets there. Apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to the family consisting of $I$ and all $K_{ij}$, and fix an infinite cardinal $\kappa$ larger than the cardinality of their disjoint union. Thus $|I|,|K_{ij}|\leq\kappa$, and $\kappa$ depends only on $X$ and the chosen covers, and is a cardinal in $\mathcal V$. Nothing asserts that an intersection is affine or that any cover is finite. The empty scheme is allowed: all covers can be empty and the bound is still infinite.

source.place: Tag 077N, lemma-colimit-kappa, first paragraph (choice of covers and cardinal); affine basis is Schemes Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens

proof.text:
Fix a quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$. Put $A_i=\mathcal O_X(U_i)$, $B_{ijk}=\mathcal O_X(V_{ijk})$, $M_i=\mathcal F(U_i)$, and $M_{ijk}=\mathcal F(V_{ijk})$. Restriction is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](2). The canonical, natural affine restriction isomorphisms are
$$M_i\otimes_{A_i}B_{ijk}\simeq M_{ijk}\simeq M_j\otimes_{A_j}B_{ijk},\qquad m\otimes b\mapsto b\,m|_{V_{ijk}}.$$
Indeed apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] to the identity morphism and the nested affine opens; identify $\mathrm{id}^*\mathcal F$ with $\mathcal F$ using [def-pc-module-pullback]. Since tensors are finite sums of pure tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], for each $i,j,k,m\in M_i$ choose a finite subset $T_{ijk}(m)\subset M_j$ and coefficients $b_t\in B_{ijk}$ with $m|_{V_{ijk}}=\sum_{t\in T_{ijk}(m)}b_t\,t|_{V_{ijk}}$. Choice is over a set, and no bound on the sizes of the rings or modules is required.

source.place: Tag 077N, lemma-colimit-kappa, second paragraph and its finite-support choices; Schemes Tag 01I9, lemma-widetilde-pullback

proof.text:
Start with any family $S_i^{(0)}\subset M_i$ with $|S_i^{(0)}|\leq\kappa$. Recursively set
$$S_j^{(n+1)}=S_j^{(n)}\cup\bigcup_{i\in I,\ k\in K_{ij},\ m\in S_i^{(n)}}T_{ijk}(m).$$
Assuming the bounds at stage $n$, the triples $(i,k,m)$ for fixed $j$ inject, after choices of injections into a set of size $\kappa$, into $\kappa^3$. Each chosen $T_{ijk}(m)$ is finite, so its elements can be indexed by natural numbers. Thus the new union has size at most $\kappa^3\cdot\aleph_0\leq\kappa$, using $\kappa\cdot\kappa=\kappa$ from [lem-sfb-infinite-cardinal-square]. Including $S_j^{(n)}$ does not change this bound. Induction proves the bound at every finite stage and the recursion makes the families increasing.

source.place: Tag 077N, lemma-colimit-kappa, third paragraph, the operation on families and its cardinal estimate

proof.text: Set $S_i^\infty=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbf N}S_i^{(n)}$. An enumeration of the stages and an injection of each stage into $\kappa$ bound this union by $\aleph_0\cdot\kappa\leq\kappa$, again by [lem-sfb-infinite-cardinal-square]. If $m\in S_i^\infty$, it belongs to a stage $n$, so $T_{ijk}(m)\subset S_j^{(n+1)}\subset S_j^\infty$. In particular every restriction of a generator in $S_i^\infty$ lies in the $B_{ijk}$-span of the restrictions of $S_j^\infty$. Symmetry of the covers and applying the same assertion with $i,j$ reversed give equality of these two spans inside $M_{ijk}$. This is the explicit countable closure construction; it makes no assertion that arbitrary submodules of bounded-generated modules are bounded-generated.

source.place: Tag 077N, lemma-colimit-kappa, third paragraph, countable iteration and stability of the limiting family

proof.text: Let $N_i\subset M_i$ be the $A_i$-span of $S_i^\infty$. On the affine scheme $U_i$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](1)--(3) gives $\mathcal F|_{U_i}\simeq\widetilde{M_i}$ and a map $\widetilde{N_i}\to\mathcal F|_{U_i}$ whose map on whole-affine sections is $N_i\hookrightarrow M_i$. Define $H_i$ to be its image subsheaf. The associated sheaf $\widetilde{N_i}$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image](2),(3), $H_i$ is quasi-coherent and $H_i(U_i)=N_i$ as an actual submodule of $M_i$. The counit in the affine adjunction now identifies $H_i$ with $\widetilde{N_i}$ and its section generators with $S_i^\infty$.

source.place: Tag 077N, lemma-colimit-kappa, third paragraph, construction of the affine submodules as actual quasi-coherent subsheaves; Schemes Tags 01HV, 01IA, 01IB, 01IC

proof.text: The affine restriction comparison from step 2, applied also to $H_i$, identifies $H_i(V_{ijk})\subset M_{ijk}$ with the $B_{ijk}$-span of the restrictions of $N_i$, hence of $S_i^\infty$. Its naturality for $H_i\to\mathcal F|_{U_i}$ ensures that this is the actual inclusion into $M_{ijk}$. By step 4 it equals $H_j(V_{ijk})$. The restrictions $H_i|_{V_{ijk}}$, $H_j|_{V_{ijk}}$ and $\mathcal F|_{V_{ijk}}$ are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](2). The affine counit of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] is natural: quasi-coherent subsheaves of $\mathcal F|_{V_{ijk}}$ with this same submodule of whole-affine sections are the same subsheaf, since both inclusions are the associated map of that submodule inclusion. Therefore $H_i|_{V_{ijk}}=H_j|_{V_{ijk}}$. These $V_{ijk}$ cover $U_i\cap U_j$, so the sheaf axiom, applied to local membership of sections in $H_i$ and $H_j$, gives $H_i|_{U_i\cap U_j}=H_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}$. Only images inside $M_{ijk}$ are compared; no unproved injectivity of a tensor map is used.

source.place: Tag 077N, lemma-colimit-kappa, third paragraph, equality on overlaps before gluing

proof.text:
Glue the $H_i$ and their inclusions into $\mathcal F$, using parts (2) and (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules]. The overlap identifications come from equality as subsheaves, hence satisfy the cocycle condition. The resulting map into $\mathcal F$ is injective on sections, because it is so on the cover $U_i$. Its actual range is the sheaf $\mathcal G$ with
$$\mathcal G(W)=\{s\in\mathcal F(W):s|_{W\cap U_i}\in H_i(W\cap U_i)\text{ for all }i\}.$$
This formula is a sheaf: a matching family glues in $\mathcal F$, and membership glues in each $H_i$; uniqueness is inherited from $\mathcal F$. Equality on overlaps shows $\mathcal G|_{U_i}=H_i$. Thus $\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent by the affine-local definition [pqf-def-coherent], and it is $\kappa$-generated on this cover by the images of the sets $S_i^\infty$. In particular it contains every original seed $S_i^{(0)}$ in its sections over $U_i$.

source.place: Tag 077N, lemma-colimit-kappa, third paragraph, gluing and bounded generation; Sheaves Tags 04TN, 00AL, 00AM

proof.text: For a fixed $\mathcal F$, every actual subsheaf is determined by a family of subsets of $\mathcal F(W)$, one for each open $W\subset X$, with the inherited module operations and restrictions [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus actual subsheaves inject into the set $\prod_{W\subset X\text{ open}}\mathcal P(\mathcal F(W))$, which is small in $\mathcal V$ by [def-weil-size-convention]. The families satisfying the subsheaf, quasi-coherence and $\kappa$-generation conditions form a subset. Consequently $P_\kappa(\mathcal F)$ is small. The zero subsheaf is quasi-coherent on every affine open and generated by the empty sets, so it belongs to this poset, including when $X$ or $\mathcal F$ is zero.

source.place: Tag 077N, lemma-colimit-kappa, last paragraph, the set of bounded-generated quasi-coherent subsheaves

proof.text: For $\mathcal N,\mathcal N'\in P_\kappa(\mathcal F)$, let $\mathcal L$ be the image of $\mathcal N\oplus\mathcal N'\to\mathcal F$, $(s,t)\mapsto s+t$. The source is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-direct-sum], and its image is a quasi-coherent subsheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image]. Refine generating covers for $\mathcal N$ and $\mathcal N'$ to their pairwise intersections. On each such intersection the restrictions of their generating sections, taken together, generate $\mathcal L$: a section of the image locally is a sum of images from the two summands, and their germs are spanned by those sections. The union of two sets of size at most $\kappa$ has size at most $\kappa$, by [lem-sfb-infinite-cardinal-square]. Hence $\mathcal L$ belongs to the poset and contains both subsheaves. Together with step 8 this proves nonempty directedness.

source.place: Tag 077N, lemma-colimit-kappa, last paragraph, sums as upper bounds; Modules Tag 01BF and Schemes Tag 01LB

proof.text: For each $i$ and each $s\in M_i$, use the construction of steps 3--7 with $S_i^{(0)}=\{s\}$ and all other seeds empty. The result is a member $\mathcal G\in P_\kappa(\mathcal F)$ with $s\in\mathcal G(U_i)$. Form $C=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal N\in P_\kappa(\mathcal F)}\mathcal N$ in all module sheaves: it exists by [lem-pc-scheme-modules-grothendieck-abelian] and step 8. The inclusions give $c:C\to\mathcal F$ by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-colimit-affine-sections], $C$ is quasi-coherent and $C(U_i)$ is the directed module colimit of the $\mathcal N(U_i)$. Its map to $M_i$ is surjective by the seed construction. It is injective: every element is represented by a section of some $\mathcal N(U_i)$, and a representative mapping to zero in $M_i$ is already zero, since $\mathcal N$ is an actual subsheaf of $\mathcal F$. Therefore $c_{U_i}$ is an isomorphism for every $i$.

source.place: Tag 077N, lemma-colimit-kappa, last paragraph, exhaustion of affine sections and colimit; Modules Tag 01AH, lemma-limits-colimits, and Schemes Tag 01ID

proof.text: Since $C$ and $\mathcal F$ are quasi-coherent, naturality and invertibility of the affine counit [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](1)--(3) identify $c|_{U_i}$ with the associated map of the isomorphism $c_{U_i}$. Thus each $c|_{U_i}$ has an inverse. On an overlap these inverses agree: both are inverses of the same restricted map, and inverses are unique. Glue them by [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules](1); the two composites with $c$ are identities because they are identities on every $U_i$. Hence $c$ is an isomorphism. Transporting the colimit cocone along $c$ proves that the given inclusions into $\mathcal F$ are the asserted colimit cocone [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The cardinal was fixed in step 1 independently of $\mathcal F$, so this proves the full assertion for every scheme.

title: Uniformly bounded-generated quasi-coherent subsheaves exhaust every quasi-coherent sheaf
statement: Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. For an infinite cardinal $\kappa$, call an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal N$ $\kappa$-generated if an open cover $X=\bigcup_a U_a$ admits subsets $S_a\subseteq\mathcal N(U_a)$, each of cardinality at most $\kappa$, whose germs span every stalk of $\mathcal N|_{U_a}$ as an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. There exists an infinite cardinal $\kappa$, depending only on $X$, such that for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent], the set $P_\kappa(\mathcal F)$ of all $\kappa$-generated quasi-coherent subsheaves $\mathcal N\subseteq\mathcal F$, ordered by inclusion, is small, nonempty and directed, and the inclusions exhibit $\mathcal F$ as its colimit in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness or Noetherian hypothesis is assumed.
